title: fix(components): EmptyDescription declares the div it renders, not a p
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectui#8571

## What changed

- `packages/components/src/custom/empty.tsx` — `EmptyDescription` now declares `React.ComponentProps` of `"div"`, the element it has always rendered, instead of `React.ComponentProps` of `"p"`. One token; the element is unchanged by ruling (option 1). A short comment at the declaration records why.
- `packages/components/src/__tests__/empty-description-props-name-the-element-8571.test.tsx` — the guard (details below).
- `.changeset/empty-description-props-name-the-element-8571.md` — `@object-ui/components: patch`. Declaration-only change to the published `.d.ts`; rendered output unchanged; no call site's type-check can move (measured, below). `skip-changeset` was not applied: in this repo it is a phantom label.

Provenance, by sha: the `"p"` annotation over a `div` entered this tree in `b1fd1a80f` (2026-01-28, "Refactor component structure and add new custom components") and is verbatim upstream shadcn's `empty.tsx` (fetched from `raw.githubusercontent.com`, same shape at its line 70). The file was last touched by `1570eac37` (the base-class repair for objectui#8525); this PR is built on `e411c3e58` and re-reads the merged file.

## Siblings — measured, all consistent

`Empty`, `EmptyHeader`, `EmptyMedia`, `EmptyTitle`, `EmptyContent` each declare `"div"` and return a `div`; `EmptyValue` declares `"span"` and returns a `span`. `EmptyDescription` was the only member of the family whose declaration and element disagreed. Nothing else in the file changes.

## Call-site census on `origin/main` (`e411c3e58`)

Opening tags outside `empty.tsx`: `EmptyDescription` 43, `EmptyTitle` 42, `EmptyHeader` 1, `EmptyMedia` 1, `EmptyContent` 0, across 46 files. No site passes a `ref`; the only attributes beyond `className` are one `data-testid` (`HomePage.tsx:421`). A parser-backed scan of every `EmptyDescription` / `EmptyTitle` body found zero block-level children (85 sites; the scanner was lit-controlled on a synthetic `div` child). So the census does not indicate the element should become a `p` — and per the ruling it was not taken either way; the element stays a `div` and the last test below pins that deliberately. (Brief note: the card says PR #8569 took the count "from a handful to twenty-odd"; `origin/main` already carries 43 `EmptyDescription` sites without it — #8569 has not landed on `main` as of `e411c3e58`.)

## The measurement that changed the instrument

The card expected `type-check` (both programs) to be the instrument, with a "div-only prop accepted, nonsense prop refused" pin. I ran that matrix before writing the pin — TypeScript 6.0.3, `@types/react` 19.2.18, React 19.2.8, one narrow program extending `tsconfig.test.json` per leg, `empty.tsx` mutated on disk with the mutation proven by count and restored by state after each leg (hash equal to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty):

| leg (annotation on EmptyDescription) | type-level errors |
|---|---|
| `"p"` (the defect) | only the two controls (a span-typed ref refused; `currentTarget` refused as an input) |
| `"div"` (the fix) | identical to the `"p"` leg — the same two controls |
| `"div"` intersected with `"p"` (caricature) | identical again |
| `any` (caricature) | identity pins red, `IsAny` red, implicit-any on handlers, and the nonsense-prop `@ts-expect-error` goes unused (TS2578) |

What that means: `Equal` of `React.ComponentProps` of `"div"` and of `"p"` is TRUE under this compiler. `lib.dom` declares `HTMLDivElement` and `HTMLParagraphElement` with the same members (a deprecated `align` plus the listener overloads), so under structural identity they are one type — and so are the two props types, and even their intersection. A `p`-typed ref is accepted by the `"div"` form and a `div`-typed ref by the `"p"` form; `keyof` is identical; there is no `div`-only prop in `@types/react` at all (`HTMLAttributes` is one interface for every element). The `"p"` → `"div"` change is therefore invisible to `tsc` in every program, and to vitest through the component alone. Only the `any` caricature is type-observable.

So the guard reads the SOURCE and ties it to the DOM:

1. For every function component under `src/custom/` whose single parameter's annotation names `React.ComponentProps` of a string literal and whose root return is an intrinsic JSX element, the literal must equal the tag (compiler parser, no type-checker). A member may name exactly ONE intrinsic — that is what refuses the intersection caricature. `any` drops the member out of the judged population, and the family enumeration (all seven `Empty*` members must be judged) is what refuses that.
2. Each of the seven members is rendered and its `tagName` compared with the literal its source names — the syntactic reading is checked against the real element.
3. `EmptyDescription` renders a `div` with `data-slot="empty-description"` — the ruling pinned, so a future real-`p` change is a deliberate edit with its own card.
4. The type half, erased at runtime and checked only by `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`: identity of each member's props with the element's props, `IsAny` false, a nonsense prop under `@ts-expect-error`. Documented in the test as unable to see `"p"` vs `"div"`; it exists to refuse `any` and to spell the contract a consumer reads.
5. A dead-matcher control compiles the pre-fix shape, the fix, the intersection, `any`, a variance intersection, an `asChild`-style `Comp` root, and the bare `ComponentProps` spelling in memory and asserts each reads as intended.

The sweep also found one other disagreement under `src/custom/`: `kbd.tsx` `KbdGroup` declares `"div"` and returns a `kbd` (upstream shadcn's shape too). It is ledgered in the test as a ratchet with its own decision pending — see "Out of scope" — not fixed here: the `p` reasoning in this card's ruling does not transfer to a `kbd`, and `HTMLDivElement` and `HTMLElement` are NOT identical types, so that one may be type-observable and needs its own ruling.

## Caricature matrix against the committed fix (run, not predicted)

Each leg mutated `empty.tsx` on disk (mutation proven by counting the injected and removed text), ran the pin file under vitest plus the narrow test program under `tsc`, and restored by state under a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths:

| leg | vitest on the pin file | narrow `tsc` test program |
|---|---|---|
| fix (HEAD) | 7 passed | 0 errors |
| `"p"` (defect) | 3 failed: sweep (`EmptyDescription: p -> div`), family-source, family-render | 0 errors — confirms tsc cannot see it |
| intersection | 2 failed: sweep (`div & p -> div`), family-source | 0 errors |
| `any` | 2 failed: family-source (not judged), family-render | 3 errors: TS2344 x2, TS2578 unused `@ts-expect-error` |
| element becomes a real `p` (option 2) | 4 failed: sweep, family-source (`div -> p`), family-render, ruling pin (`P` is not `DIV`) | 0 errors |

The option-2 leg's first attempt was voided and re-run: its on-disk proof used `grep -F` with a multi-line pattern, which counts per line, so the proof mis-instrumented itself (the replacement had asserted exactly one anchor). The re-run proved the mutation with a Python count (`injected=1 anchor_remaining=0`) before measuring. Every leg's assertion was observed to fail in the leg it was written for.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components run type-check` (both programs) — green. `--listFiles` on `tsconfig.test.json`: the pin file is in the program (1803 files), `custom/empty.tsx` is in both programs, zero `packages/components/dist` entries; the pin file is absent from the source program as `tsconfig.json` excludes `__tests__`, so the type half is checked by the test program only. Dependency closure built first (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/components^...'`, 7 tasks).
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/` — 244 files, 2255 tests passed (`SUITE_EXIT=0`), run after the matrix restored the tree.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/src/__tests__/empty-description-props-name-the-element-8571.test.tsx` — 7 passed.
- eslint, narrowed and proven: the config is not type-aware (no `projectService` / `parserOptions.project` in `eslint.config.js`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict; `--print-config` shows 118 / 117 rules apply to the two changed `.ts(x)` files; `--format json` over those two files: 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, at `6eb1a930b`.
- Gates, all green: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-phantom-dependencies`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-package-self-import`, `check-published-tsconfig-tooling-exclude`, `check-unreferenced-sources`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (NOT GOVERNED). A Python scanner with a lit control found zero zero-width or control code points in the three changed files.
- `turbo ls --affected` against the base lists 31 packages (components and every consumer). Declared narrowing: only `@object-ui/components` was tested locally. Invariance: the identity measurement above (`Equal` of the two props types is TRUE on the same compiler) means no downstream program can observe the change; the full farm is CI's run.

## Out of scope — handed to the PM, not filed

- `packages/components/src/custom/kbd.tsx` — `KbdGroup` declares `React.ComponentProps` of `"div"` and returns a `kbd`. Same defect class; direction needs its own ruling (type follows element, or element becomes a `div`). Not filed by this seat: the repo-scoped REST read returned 403 for this session, and MCP `search_issues` returned `total_count: 0` for the control word `EmptyDescription` (objectui#8571's own title carries it), so its zero for `KbdGroup` is not a reading. Ledgered in the guard as a ratchet line that takes the card number once one exists.
